name: CardiacLens v9.10.347.208
notes: Could not reproduce Can's reported 100% Private lock failure in this environment, including against a full copy of his real device data (785 keys) with zero errors every time. This environment only has Chromium available, not Safari's actual rendering engine, so a real WebKit-specific behavior cannot be ruled out and could not be tested directly.

Regardless of root cause, found and fixed a real design fragility: the lock button's handler required _clSecIsConfigured() (a full re-derivation of the saved profile from localStorage) to return true before it would do anything at all. If that check ever failed for any reason on a real device, the button would do nothing with zero visible feedback -- exactly the reported symptom. The button no longer depends on that check succeeding to lock the screen; the check now only decides which screen to show after locking (the normal keyboard vs. first-time setup), wrapped in its own try/catch so it cannot block the lock action itself.

This is not a confirmed fix for a confirmed root cause. It removes a real category of silent-failure risk that matches the symptom, verified only against the versions of the app available in this sandbox.
label: SecureAccessLockButtonHardening
summary: Hardened the lock button so a failed configuration check can no longer silently block locking the app. Root cause not confirmed; this addresses a real fragility that matches the reported symptom.
fixes: Lock button (100% Private pill) no longer gated behind a silent all-or-nothing configuration check.
testing: Re-ran the full real-click, real-hit-test pill test from v9.10.347.207 against v9.10.347.208 with Can's actual real backup data (785 keys) loaded instead of synthetic data: zero page errors, pill locks correctly.

Genuinely unable to reproduce the reported failure in this environment across multiple approaches: synthetic data, real backup data, real click() with hit-test verification of no overlapping elements, real iPhone and iPhone SE viewport dimensions. This sandbox has Chromium only, not WebKit, so a real Safari-specific behavior remains a possibility that could not be tested here.

Recommended next diagnostic step if this recurs: check Google Analytics (G-H2SESQBPXQ) for js_error or js_promise_rejection events, which this app already logs automatically on any real uncaught error, including the actual message, file, line, and stack trace from the real device.
